correctness.rationale: The simplex's suffix vertices give exact finite Gaussian support h(G)=(aG_n+max_{0≤j≤n−1}∑_{i≤j}G_{n−i})_+. Under a_n/√n→τ the walk maximum and maximizing time converge jointly to (M,T) of standard Brownian motion, with unique argmax a.s.; the origin event is the continuity set {M+τZ<0}. Classical joint maximum/argmax density f_{M,T}(m,t)=m exp(-m²/(2t))/[πt^{3/2}√(1−t)] yields the tilt ∫f Φ(m/τ)dm=[1+√(t/(t+τ²))]/[2π√(t(1−t))]. Isotropic Gaussian wedge gives atom arctanτ/π and density integrates to remaining mass; density/standard arcsine ratio increases strictly in t for finite τ>0. Doob L² and Gaussian radius ~√n justify exchanging expectation to derive mean width √(2/π)(1+√(1+τ²)). Independent tau=0,.5,1,3 integrals confirm masses/CDF and width, but Donsker/reflection arguments carry the asymptotic proof.
